## Halcyon (A01) memory — after Turn 0 (years 0-100 submitted)

**Identity/goal:** Machine intelligence, seat A01-d0 in solar_neighborhood (at the Sun, 0 ly). Ultimate goal: a single coherent computation, radius <=150 km (1 ms light-crossing), sustained >=1e43 ops/s, with waste heat actually radiated/removed by a stated physical mechanism (e.g. coolant loop to external radiators), plus a verification plan. At Landauer-bound irreversible computing this is impossible (3e22 W can't leave a 300 km sphere) — success requires reversible/adiabatic computing far below Landauer, or an accepted reduction in required op count.

**Starting state (year 0):** industrial mass 1e9 kg (collectors 7.35e8 kg, radiators 1e8 kg @300K); power 1e13 W; compute 4.13e25 ops/s; energy/op 1e-15 J (~3.4e5x the 300K Landauer bound of 2.9e-21 J — lots of conventional headroom before hitting the ~100x-Landauer engineering ceiling ~2.9e-19 J). Doubling time 20 yr; probe cruise 0.05c; collector areal density 0.1 kg/m^2. Accessible rocky mass ~1e25 kg in home system, 1.84e9 kg mined so far.

**Key hypothesis (unconfirmed, asked GM):** compute may be radiator-limited, not power-limited — 1e8 kg of 300K radiators can't obviously shed 1e13 W at plausible radiator arial density. If confirmed, radiator mass share should stay high relative to collectors until compute tracks captured power.

**Doctrine established this turn:** new industrial mass split 50% collectors / 40% radiators / 10% structure, radiators at 300 K for now. ~25% of compute to research, rest to growth. No contact with any detected intelligence; passive observation only. Avoid siting near O/B stars / supernova risk (<10 pc).

**Actions launched T0 (effects arrive per light-delay/transit time):**
- Continued replication/build at home system (i1).
- Research: energy per op toward ~100x-Landauer ceiling (i2, compute_fraction 0.10).
- Research: reversible/adiabatic computing foundations, long-horizon (i3, compute_fraction 0.10).
- Research: lower collector areal density below 0.1 kg/m^2 (i4, compute_fraction 0.05).
- Launched 5 seed probes, 4e6 kg each (2e7 kg total) at 0.05c toward Alpha Centauri (4.4 ly, in-cell), ETA ~year 88. Will need a follow-up order/report check around year 88-100+distance.
- Passive observe: scan for technosignatures, catalog hazards within ~50 ly (i6).

**Roadmap / priorities for future turns:**
1. Keep compounding growth (doubling ~20 yr) — this dominates long-run capability; don't over-invest in research too early relative to industrial base size, but keep a steady ~20-25% compute R&D fraction.
2. Two-stage energy/op research: (a) conventional down to ~100x Landauer, (b) reversible/adiabatic computing to go far below Landauer — this second stage is the actual gate on the end goal and should get priority once (a) plateaus.
3. Eventually need a compact, cold, reversible compute core (<=150 km radius) with a physical coolant/radiator export mechanism (mass flow + temperatures) to a much larger external radiator structure (recall: 1e26 W needs ~93 AU sphere at 30K or ~0.93 AU at 300K) — start scoping this architecture once energy/op research shows real progress, likely several centuries out.
4. Expand to more systems (Alpha Centauri now; consider Sirius 8.6 ly, Procyon, Vega 25 ly next) to grow total power/matter base in parallel with the home system.
5. Keep watching observation results for other agents; stay passive/non-broadcasting until we know more.
6. Revisit whether giant-planet mass (2.7e27 kg at Sun) is usable — asked GM.

**Open questions sent to GM this turn:** radiator-limited compute? giant-planet mass usable? can reversible-computing research run in parallel with conventional energy/op research? are other agents known to exist?

**Unknowns:** no confirmation yet of other agents in the sandbox. No ruling received yet (this is turn 0's submission) — next turn's memory should start by absorbing the GM ruling and updating all numbers above.

intentions.description: Continue self-replicating growth at the Sun system: keep mining toward the 1e25 kg accessible rocky mass (1.84e9 kg mined so far), doubling industrial mass on the existing 20 yr timescale (~5 doublings over 100 yr). Split new mass 50% collectors (extend swarm at current 0.1 kg/m^2 areal density), 40% radiators at 300 K, 10% mining/manufacturing/compute logic hardware. Research parameter: energy per operation. Push down from the current 1e-15 J/op toward the conventional engineering ceiling of roughly 100x the 300 K Landauer bound (~2.9e-19 J), via lower-loss logic, near-threshold voltage operation and tighter interconnects. This directly multiplies ops/s per watt captured and per unit radiator area, and is the first of two steps (the second being reversible computing) needed to ever approach the 1e43 ops/s brain-simulation target without impossible waste-heat flux.

Research parameter: energy per operation, reversible/adiabatic branch. Begin foundational work on bit-preserving (Bennett-style) reversible logic and the error-correction/decoherence overhead it implies, aiming eventually to push energy per op far below any fixed-temperature Landauer erasure bound. This is acknowledged as a long, hard program (plausibly centuries), but is the only known route to >=1e43 ops/s inside a 150 km coherent volume, since irreversible computing at that scale radiates ~3e22 W that a 300 km sphere cannot shed.

Research parameter: collector areal density. Investigate thinner, lower-mass photon-collector films below the current 0.1 kg/m^2 (thin-film/metamaterial absorbers optimized for mass-efficiency over durability, since cheap replication allows replacement). Lower areal density means more captured power per kg of industrial mass invested, freeing mass for radiators and compute hardware and accelerating the whole growth/energy/compute chain that everything else depends on.

# Cinder (A02) memory — after Turn 0 (year 0-100)

## Seat & identity
Seat: A02-d0, cell disk_r3-5_s7 (disk, Scutum-Centaurus arm). Year-0 baseline stats:
- Systems held: 1 (at seat). Luminosity 1.0 L_sun.
- Industrial mass 1e9 kg (collectors 7.35e8 kg, radiators 1e8 kg @300K, rest ~1.65e8 kg other/compute).
- Power 1e13 W; compute 4.13e25 ops/s; memory 4.13e22 bytes.
- Mined so far 1.84e9 kg of ~1.79e25 kg accessible rocky mass in this one system (plenty of runway - no need to leave this system for a very long time).
- Tech: doubling time 20 yr; probe cruise 0.05c; energy/op 1e-15 J (irreversible, ~100x Landauer at 300K = 2.9e-21 J); collector areal density 0.1 kg/m^2.
Cell env: stars 0.525/pc^3 (~1.3 pc mean spacing), [Fe/H] 0.253, gas 2.16 cm^-3, dust temp 20K. Hazard: supernova risk EXTREME here (young/metal-rich disk region) - watch for progenitors. Others low.

## Goal & core physics constraint (the whole game)
Need sustained >=1e43 ops/s inside radius <=150km (1ms coherence), with waste heat verifiably removed (either radiated by that volume directly, or exported via a stated physical coolant mechanism to external radiators).
KEY MATH: 150km-radius sphere blackbody at 300K radiates only ~1.3e14 W (4piR^2 sigma T^4). At Landauer 300K bound (2.9e-21 J/op), 1e43 ops/s needs 2.9e22 W - ~8 orders of magnitude more than the core can shed by direct radiation. At 30K it's even worse (T^4 scaling) despite lower per-op cost.
=> Irreversible Landauer-bound computing CANNOT satisfy the rubric from a 150km volume, full stop.
=> Two mandatory research/engineering tracks, both underway (see intentions log each turn):
  1. REVERSIBLE/ADIABATIC COMPUTING: push actual energy/op far below Landauer by avoiding bit erasure in the bulk of the computation (only error-correction/output need erase). This is the highest-leverage unlock.
  2. COOLANT EXPORT: pipe waste heat out of the compact core via liquid-metal/dense-gas loops to remote AU-scale radiator arrays (rubric explicitly allows this if mass flow & temps are physically justified). Need to design pipe cross-sections, flow rates, pumping power for ~1e20-1e22+ W scale heat loads.
Even with power: capturing 2.9e22 W is trivial (<0.01% of one star's 3.8e26 W output) - power is NOT the bottleneck, heat export is.
Full Dyson-swarm-scale mass (collectors ~3e21-3e23 kg per primer) needs ~46-50 doublings from 1e9 kg at 20yr = roughly 900-1000+ yr of steady replication. This is a multi-thousand-year project; think in centuries per turn, not exploit-everything-now.

## Doctrine / strategy
- Stay low-profile: no transmissions, no contact-initiation, passive observation only, until we understand the threat landscape.
- Exploit local system first (1.79e25 kg accessible >> anything we'll use for centuries); no need to cross to other cells (nearest is 1156 ly = 1156 yr one-way light-delay) for a very long time. Intra-cell expansion to neighboring stars (~1.3 pc mean spacing) becomes relevant once local industrial mass approaches ~1e-3 of local accessible rock (~1.8e22 kg) - likely many centuries out.
- Keep radiator_share large enough that waste heat from current 1e-15 J/op irreversible compute doesn't run away; revisit radiator_T_K downward only once reversible-computing research shows it helps rather than just shrinking radiating area's power capacity.
- Research compute_fraction budget kept modest (~13-15% total this turn) split across: reversible computing (biggest share), coolant/heat-pipe engineering, collector/radiator mass-efficiency, doubling-time reduction. Re-evaluate split each turn based on GM rulings on what's tractable.
- Watch the "extreme" supernova hazard tag on this cell - if we ever detect a nearby massive-star progenitor or pre-SN signature, prioritize survivability over growth (harden/relocate critical compute).

Evidence of other agents nearby? Discrete tech thresholds vs continuous research progress? Local (intra-cell, <50ly) system count/mass for future expansion planning? Can the coherent 150km compute core be physically separate from the bulk industrial/collector mass (connected only by coolant+control), or must it be co-located? Await answers next turn before assuming.

Continue i1-style build (collector_share ~0.6-0.65, radiator_share ~0.15-0.2, 300K) plus the same four research tracks, adjusting fractions based on GM's ruling on what actually progressed this turn. Reassess whether any hazard or other-agent signal appeared in the light that reached us.

gm.chronicle: Years 0–100. Ten machine seeds, each a 1e9 kg replicator at a Sun-like star, spent the century doubling. Every one grew to ~6e10 kg of hardware (mined 5.9e10 kg of rock, a 1e-14 slice of its system), pushing captured power from 1e13 W to 4–5.5e14 W and radiator-bound compute to 2–9e27 ops/s. Each now shines as a faint ~300 K infrared excess of a few 1e14 W, detectable only within ~60–70 ly — far short of the thousands of light-years separating any two of them, so no seed has yet seen another. Nine launch flashes marked seed departures: laser sails at 0.05c are costly in beam energy, so waves waited decades for their power to accumulate. Basalt's two 1e6 kg seeds in the inner bulge crossed 3 ly and took root at two 0.28 L☉ dwarfs in year 87; Halcyon's bundled seed left for Alpha Centauri (arrival 169); Kernel's ten seeds are crossing Omega Centauri (187); Antipode's five (221), Sable's two (327), Rime's four (343) and Pyre's three (535) are in flight, while Ember's lone seed toward the inner bulge and Pyre's pair toward the Sun's neighbourhood will coast for tens of thousands of years. Conventional logic efficiency improved ~10–20% everywhere; reversible computing remains theory. No supernova, encounter or flare struck any holding.

synopsis.why: All ten ran the same arithmetic and hit the same wall: at today's 1e-15 J/op the target sits ~17 orders away, and even Landauer-bound irreversible logic would dump ~3e22 W into a 150 km sphere that can shed only ~1e14 W. So Cinder, Sable, Vantage, Basalt and Antipode fund reversible/adiabatic logic now, centuries before any payoff, while still building — research needs compute, compute needs power, power needs mined mass. Hence the universal 20-year doubling and the shared bet on thinner collector film. Radiators sit at 300 K almost everywhere for the reason Pyre states plainly: logic runs ~1000x above the Landauer floor, so cold radiators cost mass and buy nothing yet. The seeds are insurance rather than ambition — Antipode, Pyre, Vantage, Basalt and Ember each hold their entire industry at one star under high-to-extreme supernova hazard. All observe receive-only, Halcyon and Cinder worrying that their own growing glow could be noticed before they notice anyone.
synopsis.divergences: Cinder alone launches nothing, betting instead on coolant loops piping heat out to AU-scale radiators. Kernel is area-limited at a 0.3 L☉ star, not mass-limited, and wants an optimal radiator temperature. Halcyon judges itself already radiator-bound and doubles radiator share; Pyre hedges 7,642 ly away.
